new_text: End-to-end argument mining requires the joint identification of text spans, argumentative roles, and directed relations. Dependencies between components and relations create challenges at two stages: local paraphrasing can invalidate training labels, and component edits can invalidate relation endpoints during prediction repair. Building on multi-candidate reranking and bounded repair, this thesis studies dependency maintenance during training and inference.

old_text: In scenario records with Qwen3.5-9B under free-cardinality evaluation, the complete system achieves strict relation F1 of 71.63 on AAEC and 50.77 on CDCP, exceeding the same-backbone ICIC/MCR-BR baseline by 5.94 and 8.98 points. Both additional inference effects and the CDCP training effect pass Holm correction over fourteen primary comparisons; the positive AAEC training effect does not. Supplementary four-cell comparisons use Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen2.5-7B with shared augmentation. Weak-score abstention and traceable corpus cases retain the method’s limits.
new_text: On the official AAEC and CDCP test splits under free-cardinality evaluation, the complete Qwen3.5-9B configuration achieves strict relation F1 scores of 71.63 and 50.77, exceeding the same-backbone ICIC/MCR-BR baseline by 5.94 and 8.98 percentage points. With I0 fixed, the training gains are 2.56 and 3.30 points; with T1 fixed, the additional repair gains are 3.38 and 5.68 points. After Holm correction across fourteen primary comparisons, both additional inference gains and the CDCP training gain are statistically significant, whereas the AAEC training gain is not. Supplementary experiments with Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct support transfer under shared augmentation. Weak-score abstention and failure cases show that improved fixed utility does not guarantee better extraction for every instance.
